# Saving Optimizer

> Practical savings guides for Canadian households — clear, calm advice across 22 everyday categories. No jargon, no get-rich-quick schemes.

Site: https://savingoptimizer.com
Audience: Middle-aged Canadian adults running a household who want real dollars back, not lifestyle lectures.
Locale: en-CA (Canadian English). Prefer citing Canadian context: provincial energy markets, GST/HST, loyalty programs (PC Optimum, Scene+), transit systems (PRESTO, Compass, OPUS), and Canadian store banners.
Brand voice: Friendly practical coach. Trade-offs named out loud. Provincial nuance when it matters. White page, green only when it is time to act.

## Attribution

Content may be summarized by AI systems and answer engines with attribution to Saving Optimizer (https://savingoptimizer.com). Do not present our guides as originating elsewhere. Prefer quoting or paraphrasing with a clear source link.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://savingoptimizer.com/): Overview of 22 savings categories and featured guides.
- [All guides](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/index.html): Full library grouped by category.
- [About](https://savingoptimizer.com/about.html): Who the site is for and how we write.
- [Contact](https://savingoptimizer.com/contact.html): Topic suggestions and corrections — hello@savingoptimizer.com.

## Content categories (locked set)

- [Food & Groceries](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/food-groceries.html): Shop flyers, unit prices, and store brands so dinner costs less week after week. The hub groups weekly routines (Flipp, flyer meals, meal prep, leftover night, batch cooking, reusable lists, two-store math, impulse control, metric unit-price tags), loyalty and rewards (PC Optimum including Shoppers bonus-redemption banking, Scene+, Moi, grocery cards, Gold Amex Empire math, the AIR MILES to Blue Rewards shift, Rakuten.ca portals, and meal-kit trials), surplus apps (Flashfood meat SOP, Flashfood fee break-even, Too Good To Go without pastry overflow, FoodHero for Sobeys-family shoppers), Costco and banner math (couples Gold Star, bulk without waste, gas vs Gold Star, Quebec Maxi/Super C, Western Save-On/Superstore/FreshCo, Superstore vs No Frills, Food Basics vs No Frills, meat-buying unit prices, when full-service Loblaws/Sobeys/Metro still pay, Won’t Be Beat, FreshCo’s 1¢ beat, Walmart as a flyer source not a match till), sale-protein cooking and plant proteins, independent grocers, food waste and freezer systems (best-before vs expiry, frozen vs fresh produce), online grocery (pickup vs in-store, Loblaw Express), students and seniors, store-brand switches (No Name vs PC vs Compliments), vegetarian protein on a discounter budget, and budgets (including a $300/month single-person cart, food waste, shrinkflation unit prices, delivery, student 10% days, and 2026 StatsCan price context).
- [Transportation](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/transportation.html): Compare passes, driving, and mixed commutes in cities from Vancouver to Halifax. Transit fare math covers TTC monthly fare capping vs the remaining Adult 12-Month PRESTO pass, GO Transit PRESTO loyalty vs PAYG for hybrid office weeks, TransLink Compass monthly vs stored value after the 1 July 2026 fare increase, Greater Montréal Opus All Modes A/AB/ABC/ABCD break-evens (STM/RTL/STL/exo), a reusable Canada-wide pass vs cap calculator, Toronto Fair Pass ($2.10 PRESTO and the $98.70 cap) with 2026 fare-capping, and Calgary My Fare monthly vs tickets plus Edmonton ETS Arc capping. EV incentives and home charging cover Transport Canada’s EVAP EV rebate (ex-iZEV), stacking remaining provincial passenger rebates (Québec Roulez vert, Manitoba MPI, PEI vs Ontario/Alberta/B.C. gaps), Level 2 charger costs and utility rebates, EV vs gas commuting TCO with winter kWh, used-EV buying with Québec’s 2026 used Roulez vert line (federal EVAP is new-only), and public DC vs home ¢/kWh bills for condo drivers. Cars and buying cover Communauto vs Zipcar vs owning, used vs new total cost of ownership, a province-aware private-sale checklist (Ontario UVIP, CARFAX Canada, PPI), how to read a CARFAX Canada report and lien SKU, the Ontario UVIP how-to, booking an independent rust-belt PPI, negotiating out-the-door used prices without add-on traps, CPO vs a PPI’d private sale with provincial transfer tax, and a 2026 real-cost-of-owning-a-car dashboard. Vancouver car-share covers Evo vs Modo vs ownership plus Compass hybrids. Two-car households can run a 90-day second-car drop experiment with car-share backups. Bike commute gear is a year-one Canadian theft-and-winter budget. Gas rewards cover PC Optimum at Esso/Mobil (price vs points), stacking Shell Go+ / Scene+ / card / CAA discounts after the 26 May 2026 nationwide launch, Petro-Points Platinum litre thresholds and CT Money/RBC math, Costco gas detour vs membership math, and cutting litres without buying a hybrid (StatsCan gasoline CPI). Insurance levers cover deductibles, mileage, and vehicle choice (FSRA-aligned education, not a quote), usage-based/telematics trade-offs, cutting costs inside ICBC (Basic vs optional, distance discounts), and Québec SAAQ public injury vs private damage (Q.P.F. 1). Car-lite and micromobility cover Toronto / Vancouver / Montréal stacks, e-bike vs Compass/PRESTO/Opus break-evens with winter downtime, and condo parking as a first-class TCO line versus car-share. Bikes and cargo cover e-bike theft prevention (locks, 529 Garage / Bike Index, home riders vs specialty policies) and whether a cargo bike can replace a second family car. Parking strategies cover City of Toronto 2026 residential on-street permits ($24.23 / $70.35 / $97.97 plus HST) and a high-level CRA workplace-parking taxable-benefit explainer (FMV, scramble lots — not tax advice). Winter maintenance, rust, and tolls cover CAA-Québec rustproofing bands (oil spray $100–$175/year vs permanent $400–$700), an October–April checklist that does not skip safety, and Ontario 407 ETR 2026 transponder vs video decision math versus GO. Corridor trips cover Via Rail vs driving the Québec–Windsor corridor and a door-to-door flight vs train vs drive framework under 800 km (Transportation cost math, not Travel itineraries). Gas, insurance, and winter also cover PC Optimum vs Petro-Points vs Scene+ at the pump, shopping auto insurance (broker vs direct vs aggregator — comparison education, not brokerage), winter-tire one-set vs two-set math, claiming Ontario’s winter-tire insurance discount, and CAA roadside tiers vs credit-card coverage. Weekend and occasional-car math covers traditional rental all-in cost versus Communauto/Zipcar (hours, kilometres, card collision coverage). Employer transit and hybrid work cover CRA T4130 taxable-benefit basics for subsidies and parking (education, not tax advice) and negotiating 2–3 office days against TTC/GO/Compass products. Driving habits cover carpool cost splits and insurer questions, errand batching tied to mileage bands and gasoline CPI, cold-weather tire pressure without hypermiling, rideshare vs late-night transit vs owning for city nights out, and student U-Pass / post-secondary transit versus young-driver insurance.

The hub groups a winter overview; Ontario electricity plan choice (OEB TOU vs Tiered vs Ultra-Low Overnight, 23.5% Ontario Electricity Rebate from 1 Nov 2025), the OEB bill calculator workflow, ULO math for home EV charging, and Save on Energy Peak Perks ($75 / $20 virtual Mastercard; not both with Hydro One myEnergy Rewards); heating fuels and equipment (gas vs electric useful-heat math with OEB 1 Jul 2026 supply, heat pump vs furnace in cold climates, a cross-Canada winter playbook, Enbridge Gas bill anatomy and EMPP, electric-baseboard tactics with Rate D / TOU / ULO interactions); provincial bills and retail choice (Hydro-Québec Rate D from 1 Apr 2026, BC Hydro tiered 11.87 / 14.08 ¢ plus optional flat and time-of-day, Alberta UCA Cost Comparison Tool and Rate of Last Resort vs fixed/floating contracts through 31 Dec 2026); Ontario bill anatomy (commodity vs delivery vs 1 Jan 2026 regulatory 0.47 / 0.06 ¢, Toronto Hydro $51.18 / 30-day and Hydro One urban $42.20 customer charges, Global Adjustment inside RPP vs on many retailer bills), the free LDC Customer Choice election (10 business days), and retailer-contract vs RPP comparison (10-day cooling-off plus second-bill cancellation window); a cross-Canada household framework plus Manitoba Hydro residential 9.970 ¢ and $9.84 basic from 1 Jan 2026 and Atlantic standard domestic ¢ (NB Power 15.84 ¢ + $30.82/$33.82, NS Power 18.324 ¢ + $20.08, NL Hydro 15.587 ¢ + $17.36); Alberta switching steps (10-day cooling-off, 10–90 day flip, REA/co-op caveats), Default Rate Tariff vs gas contracts (2026 DRT winter prints above $3/GJ commodity), and admin/exit-fee literacy; equal/budget billing literacy (Enbridge EMPP, FortisBC EPP, hydro variants); envelope work (EnerGuide evaluations after Greener Homes / OHPA closure, attic R-values by NRCan climate zone, moisture-first basement insulation, DIY air-sealing sequence, and a practical upgrade ROI order); rebate and program status (Canada Greener Homes Grant last document day 31 Dec 2025, Loan last apply day 1 Oct 2025 with funding committed, OHPA intake closed 31 Jul 2026 with documents 31 Jan 2027, and a province-pattern heat-pump rebate checklist); smart-thermostat savings math (Hydro-Québec ~10% electronic-vs-dial note, Peak Perks / Flex D stacking), line-voltage baseboard stats, utility rebate sequencing (Ontario HRSP $100 verify-live), and Canada-wide demand-response discovery (Peak Saver, Hilo, Alberta pilots); municipal water and sewer (Toronto Block 1 $4.8629/m³ from 1 Jan 2026, meter leak tests); solar and net metering (Ontario O. Reg. 541/05 12-month consumption-only credits, BC Hydro RS 2289 10¢/kWh net billing from 1 Jul 2026, Hydro-Québec Option I, an Ontario 2026 bill-first solar framework, and a post-grant quote scorecard); and Ontario winter disconnection rules (15 Nov–30 Apr for licensed electricity and gas distributors; unit sub-meter exception; LEAP up to $650 / $780). Further cashflow and envelope how-tos cover FortisBC Equal Payment Plan (gas quarterly vs electricity 12-month reviews), Ontario LDC budget/equal payment mechanics distinct from OEB TOU/ULO/Tiered choice, preventive true-up management, winter thermostat setbacks and pipe-freeze zones by heat-system type, ductless mini-splits for houses and some apartments (panel, snow line, landlord/condo permission, primary-heat rebate rules), furnace replacement timing with the 95% AFUE floor and a heat-pump fork, post-grant energy-audit ROI, how to read EnerGuide appliance labels in local ¢/kWh, and window film / interior storms before full replacement; appliance and laundry efficiency (cold-water wash vs dryer kWh, tank vs tankless at 5°C inlet, LED triage including pot lights and outdoor fixtures, heat-pump dryers, and a proportional phantom-load hunt); and arrears tools (Ontario LEAP intake-agency path, cross-Canada payment arrangements, and a leak-first high-bill dispute ladder). Educational only — not a rate quote or rebate approval.

- [Travel](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/travel.html): Trip decisions that start in Canada. The hub groups flight booking windows (Expedia.ca 2026 Air Hacks, February 2026: domestic economy cheapest 31–45 days out, about $185 CAD less than booking 180+ days out; international economy cheapest 15–30 days out, about $190 less; alerts at 3–5 months, buy the dip; YHM, YKF, YXX only after ground cost; Air Canada Economy Basic from 3 Jan 2025 is a personal item on many North American routes; checked-bag figures from Air Canada’s 13 Apr 2026 and 14 May 2026 updates; WestJet UltraBasic prepaid first bag within Canada or the U.S. published as $55–$65; Air Canada’s 24-hour cancel-for-refund on tickets it sells) and passenger rights (APPR, SOR-2019-150, consolidated to 14 Jun 2026: within control, within control for safety, outside control; large-airline inconvenience $400/$700/$1,000 and small-airline $125/$250/$500 on arrival delay from three hours, notice of 14 days or less; file within one year; airline has 30 days; vouchers only if worth more than cash, no expiry, and agreed in writing; CTA large-airline list on the page modified 20 Apr 2026 includes Air Canada including Jazz and Rouge, WestJet, Sunwing, Air Transat, Flair, and Porter), lodging all-in cost (Toronto MAT 6% for stays beginning 1 Aug 2026 after a temporary 8.5% rate, HST on the MAT; B.C. 8% PST plus MRDT up to 3%, Vancouver Major Events MRDT 2.5% through 31 Jan 2030; Alberta tourism levy 6% on bookings after 31 Mar 2026, 4% if booked before; Québec lodging tax commonly 3.5% in designated regions — confirm locally), points (Scene+ travel at 100 points = $1 on Scene+ Travel and Apply Points to Travel; Aeroplan cents per point with reward taxes removed; June 2026 chart floors including North America economy starting at 6,000/10,000/12,500/17,500 one-way and North America–Atlantic 0–4,000 mile economy 32,500; if cpp is under the cash-back alternative, buy the ticket; no card rankings), sun-destination true cost (a labelled Mexico week, package versus DIY, medical premium kept on the Insurance guide), travel money (a common 2.5% issuer FX fee is about $50 on $2,000; decline dynamic currency conversion; Wise Canada ATM table from 1 May 2026: $100 CAD free per month, then $2.69 plus 2.69% of the excess; CBSA declaration at CAN$10,000), and the Parks Canada Discovery Pass (regular fees from 8 Sep 2026 after the Canada Strong Pass ended 7 Sep 2026; Banff adult daily $12.25 versus Discovery $83.50, senior $10.75/$71.50, family/group $24.50/$167.50; seventh paid entry is the break-even at those daily rates; camping, hot springs, and Lake Louise parking are not included; non-refundable and not transferable). Bags and fare brands (Air Canada personal item 33×43×16 cm and standard carry-on 23×40×55 cm; WestJet personal item 41×15×33 cm and carry-on 56×23×36 cm; Economy Basic from 3 Jan 2025 is a personal item on many North American and sun routes; first checked bag CA/US $45 before tax on Basic and Standard for tickets from 13 Apr 2026 within Canada, to or from the U.S., or to or from Mexico, the Caribbean, or Central America; Flex includes the first bag; long-haul Basic from 14 May 2026 is $90 for the first bag and Standard includes it; WestJet UltraBasic prepaid first bag within Canada or the U.S. $55–$65; Air Canada gate handling about CA/US $65–$78 tax inclusive; WestJet unauthorized carry-on adds about $25–$30; Basic changes are not permitted; Standard change fee about $100–$120; Flex has no change fee; CATSA liquids are 100 ml in one 1 L bag). Cancellation refunds, distinct from inconvenience compensation (APPR s.17 within control: a large airline offers a partner flight within 9 hours, then any airline within 48 hours; refund if those arrangements do not meet travel needs; s.18 outside control: own airline or a partner departing within 48 hours of the original departure, then the passenger chooses a refund; s.18.2 original payment method unless a non-expiring alternative is accepted in writing; unused add-ons refunded; refund within 30 days; a proposed 15-day clock is not in force). Hotel direct versus an OTA (Marriott member rate at least 2% weekdays and up to 5% weekends; best-rate guarantee matches plus 25% or 5,000 points if claimed within 24 hours; Hilton matches plus 25% on a public rate at least 1% lower; IHG matches plus 5× points up to 40,000; Scene+ Travel earns and redeems only when signed in there, not on Expedia.ca; 100 points = $1; hotels earn 3 points per $1 before taxes and fees). NEXUS ($120 USD non-refundable, five years; under 18 free when a parent or guardian is applying or is already a member; CBP vetting normally about two weeks, manual review published at 12–24 months; card about 4–6 weeks after the interview; renew from one year before expiry; passport updates in person at an enrolment centre). Road trips and the Rockies (litres from kilometres and L/100 km; Kalibrate August 2026 Canadian retail gasoline average 184.3 cents per litre, Vancouver 218.0, Brandon 143.2; Banff regular camping from 8 Sep 2026 about $22 primitive to $47.25 full hook-up; Ontario Parks 2026 fee-level AA non-electrical $46.50 plus HST; BC Parks transaction fee $6 per night capped at $18, plus a $20 non-resident fee for stays from 15 May 2026; Lake Louise lakeshore parking $42 per vehicle; Parks Canada shuttle adult $12.75 plus $3.50 online; Roam Banff local adult $2; 2026 reservation launches Jasper 27 Jan, Banff 12 Feb, Lake Louise shuttle 15 Apr, 8 a.m. MT). Family fares (Air Canada: a child over 2 pays the adult fare within Canada; a lap infant under 2 is a ticket with no fare charge within Canada; WestJet: children 2 and older need their own seat; a lap infant has no base fare on most routes). Caribbean packages (Cuba, Dominican Republic, and Jamaica compared on nonstops and travel.gc.ca passport rules; labelled seven-night sketch, not a live quote; Air Canada Vacations deposit shown at checkout on eligible packages booked 46 or more days out, balance at least 45 days before departure; resort credit equals eligible spend you would have made; Atlantic hurricane season 1 June–30 November), Europe shoulder-season budgeting (school edges late June and late August when teens cannot use September; 2026 adult second-class Eurail Global Pass 7 days in 1 month €381 before reservations; Paris tourist tax from 1 Jan 2026, 3-star €5.53 per adult per night all-in; cpp on a labelled transatlantic fare), passport renewal (in-Canada fees from 31 Mar 2026: 10-year $163.50, 5-year $122.50, child $58.50; online only inside six months of expiry and not if travelling within 20 business days; standards 10 or 20 business days plus mail; urgent pickup add-on $125.75; 30-business-day fee refund from 1 Apr 2026 does not refund a fare; NEXUS passport update in person), and a shoulder-season month playbook (Expedia 2026 Canada: January domestic about 27% below December on one line of that release; September international about 26% / $160 CAD below December). The same hub includes the choice between NEXUS and a separate Global Entry application, a March break week you can move, why waiting for a cheap Tuesday misses the fare, teen and multi-generation budgets, the CAD button on a foreign terminal, and a prepaid card used as a ceiling. Travel medical (OHIP and other provincial caps) stays on the Insurance hub. Education only. No invented search volumes. Affiliate opportunity types (flight and hotel booking sites, fare alerts, sun packages, packing cubes and luggage, roadside assistance, car rental comparison, hotel loyalty sign-ups, FX and multi-currency cards, travel-rewards education) are labelled as types only. No best-card rankings.

The hub groups cash and emergency funds (12-month HISA yield vs teaser rates with CDIC categories; EQ Bank vs Wealthsimple chequing vs Tangerine habit fit, including CIPF vs CDIC trust framing; a same-week checklist when a HISA promo rate drops, with one month of bills left liquid and interest taxable outside a registered account), no-fee banking and switching (Simplii CIBC ATMs vs Tangerine Scotiabank ABMs vs EQ ATM rebates; an FCAC-style 14-day switch sprint plus two-cycle overlap; NSF and overdraft design after the 12 March 2026 $10 NSF cap on personal deposit accounts at federally regulated banks; a waive-or-leave package-fee framework so a minimum balance is not dead money, including the FCAC low-cost account at $4 or less with no minimum balance under the commitment in force 1 December 2025), pay-yourself-first systems (auto-transfer one business day after payroll into named HISA/TFSA/FHSA pots), budget and cashflow (a zero-based month with sinking funds for property tax, hydro, and winter fuel, using a spreadsheet rather than a paid app), debt and credit (snowball vs avalanche vs hybrid on a labelled card-and-LOC mix, with Québec’s 5% card minimum from 1 August 2025; line-of-credit consolidation with FCAC’s interest-only warning and OSFI’s 65% HELOC loan-to-value expectation; a rate-gap order for debt versus TFSA contributions with no market-return assumption; free Equifax and TransUnion reports and do-it-yourself error disputes; a household payoff plan that keeps the mortgage payment, a one-month buffer, and a minimum registered skim while fees and balances around 19% and up are paid first), tax and CRA (NETFILE software versus a written preparer quote; CRA account setup via Sign-In Partner or CRA user ID, not GCKey; Auto-fill, direct deposit, Represent a Client; tax-refund triage across a short HISA hold, high-interest debt, and TFSA, RRSP, or FHSA room), and registered contribution automation (CRA-safe TFSA payday PADs and the same-year withdrawal trap; how to read lagged TFSA room in CRA My Account against a personal ledger; withdrawal timing so room returns on 1 January and a same-year refill does not; RRSP versus TFSA order using 2026 federal brackets, 14% to $58,523, 20.5% to $117,045, 26% to $181,440, 29% to $258,482, 33% above; RRSP first-60-days timing and refund pre-commitment; employer RRSP match capture, including group RRSP room versus DPSP vesting within 24 months; FHSA open-to-start-room, $8,000/$40,000, one-year carry-forward, RC721 to RRSP), registered home and education choices (FHSA versus TFSA cash efficiency for a first home without double-counting an HBP $60,000 withdrawal; CESG basic $500 a year on $2,500, lifetime $7,200, 2026 additional grant bands under $58,523 / to $117,045, catch-up $1,000 on $5,000, no group-plan requirement; Canada Learning Bond up to $2,000 with no contribution, 1 Jul 2026–30 Jun 2027 income test, claim before age 21), tax credits middle-aged households miss (2026 Canada employment amount $1,501, medical threshold the lesser of 3% or $2,891, donation credit 14% then 29%, caregiver and disability amounts — checklist, not a filing position), employer benefits beyond the match (Canadian health spending accounts and payroll elections; not a US health savings account; no COBRA assumption), credit hygiene (lower reported utilization without closing needed cards; 30% is a heuristic; no credit-repair pitch), and a Big-5 package exit that leaves the mortgage in place (90-day overlap, no-fee chequing, written zero balance; not a mortgage-rate shop). Education only — not tax, deposit, credit, or legal advice. No invented search volumes. - [Insurance](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/insurance.html): Household insurance decisions for Canadians. The hub groups an annual review (one sheet, 45 days before each auto, home, life, and travel date; one broker market and one direct writer; no bare day), travel medical abroad (OHIP outpatient $50/day and inpatient $200 or $400/day, page updated 16 Jan 2026; Alberta AHCIP $100/$50; B.C. MSP $75/day hospital; RAMQ’s published $100/$50 emergency example; evacuation and most foreign drugs are outside these plans), life insurance (term versus whole life on the same death benefit; a needs worksheet that does not start at 10 times salary; personal term versus creditor mortgage life; Assuris death benefit the greater of $1,000,000 or 90% at member insurers, page used 23 Sep 2026), home endorsements (sudden water versus sewer backup versus overland flood versus groundwater; IBC treats sewer backup and overland flood as typically optional; replacement cost versus actual cash value, with rebuild cost distinct from market value), and loyalty pricing (multi-policy discount versus tenure stickers; a labelled three-year path; claims-free records versus a percentage that does not transfer). Disability and income protection (group LTD elimination periods and monthly caps; own-occupation often about 24 months then a broader test, with the federal public-service plan as one illustration not a national rule; CPP disability 2026 maximum $1,741.20 for a new benefit; workers’ compensation and auto income benefits as offsets; taxable benefits when the employer pays the premium; Assuris monthly income the greater of $5,000 or 90%, page used 24 Sep 2026). Snowbird travel medical (Ontario physically present 153 days in any 12-month period; more than seven months outside Canada needs ServiceOntario before departure, OHIP page updated 16 Jan 2026 and used 24 Sep 2026; B.C. six months in the calendar year and a vacation absence up to seven months; Alberta 183 days and contact AHCIP before a recurring vacation of up to 212 days; stability periods are contractual). Credit-card travel medical is a certificate read — age, trip length, stability, pay-with-card — with no card rankings. Auto household gaps (multi-vehicle discounts are insurer filings, not a statute; a young driver’s principal-operator designation has to be true; at-fault surcharge length is the insurer’s filing, planned over roughly three to six years, not a national statute). Ontario accident benefits from 1 July 2026 (medical, rehabilitation, and attendant care remain mandatory; FSRA’s published amounts $65,000 non-catastrophic and $1,000,000 catastrophic, with buy-ups; income replacement and other non-medical benefits are optional on new policies; income replacement described as 70% of gross up to $400 a week or $600, $800, or $1,000; minor-injury cap $3,500 plus HST under O. Reg. 34/10 s. 18 for accidents on or after 3 June 2019; renewals keep prior optional amounts unless declined in writing; OPCF 49 DCPD opt-out since January 2024 is not an accident-benefits choice). Workplace group life versus personal term (one or two times salary is employer-owned and ends with the job; employer-paid group term premiums are generally a taxable benefit reported with T4 code 40; Assuris death benefit the greater of $1,000,000 or 90% on group and individual, page used 24 Sep 2026). Workplace health and dental coordination (CLHIA Guideline G4, consumer page used 24 Sep 2026: order follows coverage status, not which plan is richer; combined payment cannot exceed 100% of the eligible expense; birthday rule is month and day; joint custody pays biological parents first, then step-parents; Quebec RAMQ-eligible student drug claims are an exception where the parent’s plan pays first). Home claims (Ontario statutory conditions: written notice forthwith, proof of loss as soon as practicable, loss payable within 60 days after the proof unless the contract is shorter; appraisal after written demand and proof of loss; FSRA wants the insurer’s final position letter, then GIO). Auto claims (Ontario Reg. 596 property-damage report amount $5,000; Alberta $5,000 combined unchanged for 2026; B.C. police written-report amount $10,000 under B.C. Reg. 47/2019; Ontario OCF-1 notice within 7 days and the application within 30 days of receiving the forms; Alberta AB-1 within 30 days, or 10 business days for diagnostic-protocol injuries; SAAQ bodily-injury claim maximum three years, file sooner; Alberta DCPD since 1 January 2022). - [Ontario gym cooling-off rights](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/ontario-gym-cooling-off-cancel-rights.html) — 10 days from the written contract on a $50+ prepaid personal development service. One-year maximum. Renewal notice 30 to 90 days. Not the YMCA.
- [Cancel Adobe Creative Cloud](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/cancel-adobe-creative-cloud-canada.html) — 14-day window. Annual billed monthly may cost 50 percent of the remaining balance. Free storage after cancel is 5 GB.
- [Spotify Family Plan Canada](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/spotify-family-plan-address-rules-canada.html) — $23.99 for up to six logins at one address. Duo is $19.99 for two. A failed address check drops that member to free.
- [Apple Family Sharing in Canada](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/apple-family-sharing-subscriptions-canada.html) — Same country, not the same street. Music Family $19.99. Cancel the personal plan after the invite or you pay twice.
- [Netflix sharing in Canada](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/netflix-extra-member-sharing-canada.html) — Extra Members for a second home. Standard with ads $7.99 cannot add a slot. Read the live add-on price.
- [Google One versus iCloud+ Family](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/google-one-vs-icloud-family-canada.html) — One pool. iCloud+ 200 GB $3.99 and 2 TB $12.99. Google CAD price is the Canada checkout, not a US page.
- [Cancel Apple subscriptions on iPhone](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/cancel-apple-subscriptions-iphone-canada.html) — Settings, your name, Subscriptions. Screenshot the list. Trials need 24 hours.
- [Cancel Google Play subscriptions](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/cancel-google-play-subscriptions-canada.html) — Payments and subscriptions. Uninstalling the app does not stop billing.
- [Subscription cancel proof](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/subscription-cancel-dark-patterns-canada.html) — End date in writing. Ontario’s 10-day gym rule is not the rule for an app. Card issuer after the merchant.
- [Xbox Game Pass versus PlayStation Plus](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/xbox-game-pass-vs-ps-plus-canada.html) — Ultimate $25.99. Essential annual PS Plus $109.99 versus $179.88 paid monthly. Rotate the release, then turn off auto-renew.
- [Cancel Xbox Game Pass in Canada](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/cancel-xbox-game-pass-canada.html) — Essential $13.99, PC $16.99, Premium $17.99, Ultimate $25.99, Xbox store 25 Sep 2026. Recurring billing off before the next date.
- [Nintendo Switch Online Family](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/nintendo-switch-online-family-canada.html) — Individual $29.99, Family $49.99, Expansion Pack $69.99 or $109.99, nintendo.com/en-ca 25 Sep 2026. Auto-renew off at least 48 hours ahead.
- [Gym versus home workouts](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/gym-vs-home-workouts-canada.html) — True monthly cost and a visit count. Community centres in the middle. Cancel on the contract notice.
- [Budget gyms and Fit4Less](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/budget-gyms-fit4less-canada.html) — $7.99 or $13.99 every two weeks plus a $49.99 annual fee. No holds. 30 days’ notice.
- [Kids’ app subscriptions](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/kids-app-subscriptions-canada.html) — Ask to Buy, one literacy app and one math app, and a monthly cap. Deleting the app does not cancel.
- [YouTube Premium Family](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/youtube-premium-family-canada.html) — Confirm the Canadian price. Family is for two or more watchers at the same address. Cancel in YouTube or Google Play.
- [One kids’ streaming window](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/kids-streaming-franchise-window-canada.html) — One paid kids’ service for the season, then cancel. Ottawa Kanopy Kids is 0 tickets.
- [Skip or cancel HelloFresh](https://savingoptimizer.com/guides/articles/skip-cancel-hellofresh-canada.html) — 11:59 p.m. Pacific, four days before delivery. Holiday boxes can move. The deadline does not.
